c: Aristotle De Anima records
Classical philosophy archives
records.d: Aristotle treated taste as one of the five senses with its own organ, the tongue: the philosophical oldest form of taste science. Flavor was data the body collected. The inquiry into how taste works is 2,300 years old.
records.h: Aristotle reasoned that taste perceived flavors dissolved in moisture, distinguishing sweet, bitter, and others by bodily effect. Observation was the instrument. The sense was mapped before it was measured.
records.mj: Established - documented Aristotelian treatment of taste as a sense.
records.t: c. 350 BCE: Aristotle Maps the Sense of Taste

c: Hanig dissertation records, 1901
Psychophysics history
records.d: In 1901, D. P. Hanig mapped regional taste sensitivities across the tongue, work later oversimplified into the 'tongue map' myth. Real finding: sensitivity varies by region. The tongue's geography was measured.
records.h: Threshold measurements for sweet, salty, sour, and bitter across tongue regions showed varying sensitivity. Later textbooks distorted this into exclusive zones. The measurement was real; the myth was the distortion.
k: Later distorted into the tongue-map myth
records.mj: Established - documented 1901 Hanig psychophysics; regional sensitivity mapping.

c: Ikeda umami records, 1908
Tokyo Imperial University archives
records.d: Kikunae Ikeda identified umami in 1908, isolating glutamate as the savory taste: a fifth basic taste. The taste palette grew. Flavor science gained a new primary.
records.h: Chemical analysis of kombu dashi isolated monosodium glutamate as the savory principle; Ikeda named the taste umami. Taste receptors would confirm it a century later. The palette went from four to five.
records.mj: Established - documented 1908 Ikeda discovery; umami and glutamate.

c: FDA aspartame approval, 1974
Food additive history
records.d: Aspartame's approval in 1974 put engineered taste in every diet soda: sweetness designed in a lab. Taste became a design material. Flavor could be invented, not just found.
records.h: The synthetic dipeptide bound sweet receptors with hundreds of times sugar's potency at near-zero calories. Food science engineered the sensation. Taste was now a specification.
records.mj: Established - documented 1974 FDA approval; engineered sweet taste.

c: Taste receptor gene papers, 2000-2001
Genetics literature
records.d: Around 2000, researchers identified the genes for sweet and umami taste receptors: taste's molecular hardware. The tongue's sensors were decoded. Flavor had a parts list.
records.h: Molecular biology located T1R receptor genes and linked them to sweet and umami perception. The signal chain from molecule to sensation was mapped. Taste became engineerable at the receptor.
records.mj: Established - documented taste receptor gene identification; molecular taste hardware.

c: Ranasinghe Digital Lollipop papers, 2011
NUS HCI research
records.d: Nimesha Ranasinghe's Digital Lollipop, shown in 2011, simulated tastes electrically on the tongue: sour, salty, bitter, and sweet from electrodes. Taste became an output device. The tongue got a display.
records.h: Controlled electrical stimulation of the tongue's regions evoked basic tastes without chemicals, with current patterns encoding the taste. The lollipop was a proof of concept. Electricity became flavor.
k: Sour, salty, bitter, sweet from current
records.mj: Established - documented 2011 NUS research; electrical taste simulation.

c: University of Tokyo Meta Cookie, 2013
AR food research
records.d: The Meta Cookie system, shown in 2013, changed perceived cookie flavor with AR visuals and scent: the eyes and nose rewrote the tongue. Flavor proved multisensory. The cookie was a display.
records.h: Head-mounted visuals plus scent delivery altered flavor perception of a plain cookie, demonstrating crossmodal taste effects. The tongue tasted what the system suggested. Perception was the interface.
records.mj: Established - documented 2013 research; AR-altered flavor perception.

c: Thermal taste interface research, 2016
Gustatory HCI literature
records.d: By 2016, researchers were mapping thermal taste: warming and cooling the tongue to modulate perceived flavor. Temperature became a taste control. The thermostat joined the flavor console.
records.h: Peltier-driven thermal interfaces shifted perceived sweetness and intensity, building on the thermal-taste phenomenon. Heat was a flavor knob. The display gained a dimension.
records.mj: Emerging - real research literature; thermal modulation of taste perception.

c: Ranasinghe Vocktail, 2017
Virtual cocktail research
records.d: The Vocktail, shown in 2017, was a virtual cocktail glass simulating flavor, color, and scent: drinking a digital drink. The cocktail became software. Taste, sight, and smell rendered together.
records.h: Electrical taste stimulation plus LED color and scent release simulated cocktail experiences in a 3D-printed glass. Multisensory rendering made the virtual drink convincing. The glass was a display stack.
records.mj: Established - documented 2017 Vocktail; multisensory virtual beverage.

c: Miyashita Norimaki Synthesizer, 2018
Meiji University records
records.d: Homei Miyashita's Norimaki Synthesizer, shown in 2018, reproduced flavors electrically: five gels on the tongue driven by currents recreated tastes. The seaweed-wrap device synthesized flavor. Taste became programmable.
records.h: Ion electrophoresis from five taste gels delivered controlled stimuli to the tongue, with programs composing flavor sequences. The device was named for sushi wrapping. Flavor synthesis left the lab for the demo table.
records.mj: Established - documented 2018 Miyashita lab device; electrical flavor reproduction.

c: Taste Buddy prototype coverage, 2020
Gustatory tech coverage
records.d: By 2020, prototypes like Taste Buddy were exploring spoon-based taste modulation for health: making bland food taste better electrically. The spoon became medical. Flavor therapy went digital.
records.h: Utensil-integrated stimulation adjusted perceived taste during eating, aimed at reducing salt and sugar needs. The meal stayed the same; the perception changed. Health met the tongue.
records.mj: Emerging - real prototypes; utensil-based taste modulation for health.

c: Miyashita Taste the TV, December 2021
TTTV demonstration records
records.d: In December 2021, Miyashita demonstrated Taste the TV: a screen that sprayed flavor onto film for licking, reproducing tastes on demand. The TV you could taste. Ten canisters synthesized the flavor.
records.h: Ten flavor canisters sprayed combinations onto a hygienic film over the screen, mixed to match the displayed food. Users licked the flavor. The display closed the loop from image to taste.
records.mj: Established - documented December 2021 demonstration; flavor-spraying TV prototype.

c: VR dining prototype coverage, 2022
Gastronomy tech reports
records.d: By 2022, VR dining prototypes were pairing virtual meals with taste simulation: eating in virtual restaurants with rendered flavor. The restaurant went virtual. Dining became a renderable experience.
records.h: Headset visuals plus taste interfaces presented courses whose flavors were partially simulated. The social ritual stayed; the kitchen shrank. Presence dining was prototyped.
records.mj: Emerging - real prototypes; VR dining with taste simulation.

c: AI flavor prediction coverage, 2023
Food science AI reports
records.d: By 2023, AI was predicting flavor from molecular structure: models proposing tasty combinations for food companies. The flavorist gained an AI colleague. Taste design went computational.
records.h: Machine-learning models trained on flavor chemistry predicted appealing combinations and substitutions. R&D cycles shortened. The palate became a dataset.
records.mj: Emerging - real industry practice; AI flavor prediction.

c: Ohio State e-Taste, 2024
Gustatory interface research
records.d: Ohio State's e-Taste, reported in 2024, sensed and reproduced tastes remotely: chemical sensors read a flavor, actuators recreated it for a distant tongue. Taste telegraphy worked in the lab. Flavor became transmittable.
records.h: Sensor arrays analyzed the source's chemistry while actuator gels delivered matched stimuli to the receiver's tongue. The loop was sense-then-render. Tele-taste left science fiction.
records.mj: Established - documented 2024 research; remote taste sensing and reproduction.

c: Taste-sharing prototype coverage, 2024
Social gustatory tech
records.d: By 2024, prototypes were letting people share tastes socially: sending a flavor to a friend's device. Taste became a message. The group chat gained a sense.
records.h: Recorded flavor profiles transmitted to paired devices rendered the taste for recipients. Sharing was asynchronous. Social media's final sense was prototyped.
records.mj: Emerging - real prototypes; social taste sharing.

c: Restaurant pilot coverage, 2025
Hospitality tech reports
records.d: By 2025, restaurants were piloting digital taste: previewing dishes' flavors before ordering, adjusting salt perception for health. The menu became interactive. Dining's digital layer arrived.
records.h: Tabletop taste interfaces let diners sample flavor profiles and tune perceived saltiness, supporting low-sodium menus. The preview reduced waste. The restaurant gained a flavor API.
records.mj: Emerging - real pilots; restaurant digital-taste interfaces.
